reuse.why: Consumers reuse getExpectedScheduleAmount, but its approximate branch reimplements the existing getApproxNumberThreshold helper from shared/rules.ts.

duplication.why: Expected-amount selection remains centralized, but the rounded 7.5% tolerance calculation duplicates an existing shared definition.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy stays in shared/schedules.ts, while API field mapping stays in server/api-models.ts.

scope.why: The edits are confined to expected schedule amounts, their consumers, and focused helper tests.

maintainability.why: The optional string operator permits API serialization and forecast normalization to omit required policy context, while duplicated tolerance arithmetic introduces another definition to maintain.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedScheduleAmount calculates tolerance inline instead of calling shared/rules.ts:getApproxNumberThreshold.

disguised_duplication.where: The duplicated tolerance expression is copied directly into getExpectedScheduleAmount rather than renamed or reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount gains optional op and an isapprox branch that bypasses getApproxNumberThreshold; API serialization and forecast normalization also retain calls without operator context.
